purpose: Fixed historical first-translation regression, not a semantic checker or new quality pass.
selectionRule: All 42 earlier actual Qwen outputs from both fixed source-grounding arms, plus all four actual translations from the last anchor study; inherited labels unchanged. No model inference, new corruption, best-result selection or relabeling.
limits: 46 related outputs are not 46 independent source cases. Synthetic source text is distinct from manual corruption: every observed translation here was actually generated. Known diagnostics and the unadopted grounded arm are not current production acceptance. Offline replay cannot measure present generation quality, recall, speed or tokens. No-confirmed-fault is not perfect translation.

cases.source: If the water vapor is associated with the planet, that would indicate that it has an atmosphere despite its scorching temperature and close proximity to its star. Water vapor has been seen on gaseous exoplanets before, but to date no atmosphere has been definitely detected around a rocky exoplanet. However, the team cautions that the water vapor could be on the star itself – specifically, in cool starspots – and not from the planet at all.
cases.observedTranslation: 如果水蒸气与行星有关联，则表明尽管其温度极高且距离恒星极近，它仍拥有大气层。此前已在气态系外行星上观测到水蒸气，但迄今为止尚未在岩石系外行星周围明确探测到大气层。然而，研究团队警告称，这些水蒸气可能源自恒星本身——具体而言是位于较冷的黑子区域——而非来自行星。

cases.source: The length of the plume was not the only characteristic that intrigued researchers. The rate at which the water vapor is gushing out, about 79 gallons per second, is also particularly impressive. At this rate, you could fill an Olympic-sized swimming pool in just a couple of hours. In comparison, doing so with a garden hose on Earth would take more than 2 weeks.
cases.observedTranslation: 羽流的长度并非唯一令研究人员着迷的特征。水蒸气喷涌而出的速率——每秒约79加仑——同样令人印象深刻。以这一速率，仅需数小时即可注满一个奥运标准游泳池。相比之下，若使用地球上的花园水管完成同样的注水任务，则需耗时超过两周。
